title: Exact augmented integral quotient Roos functor on homotopy categories
statement: Fix a prime ell and a finite extension E of Q_ell [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme T [def-pc-scheme]. Let M be the sheaves of modules over the completed integral coefficient ring on the small pro-etale site of T [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Write q: C(M) -> K(M) for the homotopy quotient and Qh: K(M) -> D(M) for the derived quotient [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The ordinary quotient Roos functor R and its specified augmentation u [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] have an exact homotopy descent H: K(M) -> D(M), with coherent integer shifts, an isomorphism e: q H -> R Q and a shift-compatible natural transformation beta: Qh -> H. For every complex P, the canonical comparison Q(P) -> Qh(q(P)), followed by beta(q(P)) and e(P), equals Q(u(P)). The site and coefficient universes are independent. This assertion concerns homotopy categories only: it neither asserts that R preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms nor constructs its derived completion.

proof.text: Construct moduleLevel as the specified ordinary quotient reduction followed by scalar restriction. Assemble the actual module transitions into moduleTower, an additive functor to module-valued towers, and the quotient units into its natural augmentation. The tensor-generator uniqueness theorem transition_existsUnique identifies its degreewise transitions with IntegralOnSlice.transition. The generic SequenceComplex comparison then identifies the transposed degreewise module tower with IntegralOnSlice.tower. The arrow-cofiber/cone map identity gives roosComparison between the resulting signed Roos functor and the prescribed ordinary quotient Roos functor.

proof.text: Apply the stated compatible-homotopy theorem to the image under moduleTower of a cochain homotopy. Its localized Roos maps are equal, so Quotient.lift constructs H on the homotopy category. Quotient.liftCommShift supplies coherent integer shifts and a shift-compatible factorization isomorphism. The cone-calculus theorem supplies a cone comparison preserving inclusion and the signed last arrow. Combine it with Mathlib mappingCone.mapTriangleIso for the additive module tower. Every distinguished homotopy triangle is isomorphic to such a mapping-cone triangle; the factorization and these two triangle comparisons identify its image under H with a distinguished derived mapping-cone triangle.

proof.text: The module augmentation gives an actual cone over each degreewise tower and hence its zero-second-coordinate Roos augmentation. The stated augmentation naturality and signed shift-augmentation identities show this is a natural transformation commuting with integer shifts. Descend its localization through Quotient.natTransLift, using quotientCompQhIso and the inverse factorization isomorphism. Faithfulness of whiskering with the full homotopy quotient detects the shift identity. For normalization, the tensor-generator formula identifies the transported module augmentation with the specified IntegralOnSlice.augmentation. The naturality calculation for the explicit mapping-cocone lift with zero second cochain identifies the transported Roos augmentation with roosUnit. Cancel the quotient and factorization isomorphisms to obtain the required component equality.

lean.statement:
theorem integralQuotientRoos_homotopy
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}) :
    ∃ (H : HomotopyCategory (Mod l E T none) (.up ℤ) ⥤ D l E T none)
      (_ : H.CommShift ℤ)
      (e : HomotopyCategory.quotient (Mod l E T none) (.up ℤ) ⋙ H ≅
        roos l E T none ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (β : DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ H),
      H.IsTriangulated ∧ NatTrans.CommShift β ℤ ∧
        ∀ P : Cx l E T none,
          (DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso (Mod l E T none)).inv.app P ≫
            β.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (Mod l E T none) (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
              e.hom.app P = DerivedCategory.Q.map (roosUnit l E T none P)
